This post provides an independent comparison of current routers and looks at how today's routers compare with single models on quality and cost.

Its immediate predecessor is the best-selling nonmobile game of all time. The game's release is causing other entertainment companies to delay products until next year because they know GTA VI will suck up the planet's attention for most of November. It will almost certainly be the most expensive video game ever created. This article looks at how Rockstar Games built what is expected to be the biggest video game blockbuster of all time.

The AI lab is currently pursuing what may become the largest-ever initial public offering. Its IPO could value the company at $2 trillion. The San Francisco company is expected to begin trading as early as next month. A successful launch from Anthropic could reopen the door for other listings and provide a vote of confidence for the industry.

articles.headline: 28 Miles and Counting: NASA's Perseverance Rover Sets a Mars Driving Record
articles.blurb: NASA's Perseverance rover has now driven 28.1 miles on Mars' surface, surpassing the distance that Opportunity covered from 2004 to 2018. Perseverance landed on Mars in February 2021 and has been traveling in and around the Jezero Crater since. It was set to surpass the driving record back in August, but it came across some interesting rocks, so it dawdled for two months. Perseverance most likely still has many miles to go in the coming years. This article contains some of the highlights from its drive so far.

articles.headline: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation
articles.blurb: Two NASA missions are on track to launch to Venus in the early 2030s. The Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging (DAVINCI), which will send a parachute-assisted descent probe through Venus' atmosphere, is now scheduled for launch in December 2030. The Venus Emissivity, Radio science, InSAR, Topography, And Spectroscopy (VERITAS) mission will launch in November 2032 to map the Venusian surface by radar from orbit. The European Space Agency is building an orbiter for launch to Venus in 2032, and Rocket Lab plans to launch a privately funded probe as soon as next year to search for signs of organic material in the planet's clouds.

articles.headline: Code you didn't write
articles.blurb: Being able to tell clean code from messy code is still useful, but it's becoming something that tools can help with. Knowing what shape a program should have before anyone writes it is something AI still can't do yet. The best way to get better at AI coding might be to spend more time thinking about problems and less time thinking about prompts. The programmers that get the most out of these tools already knew what they wanted.

articles.headline: Agentic Verification
articles.blurb: Giving AI agents a way to independently verify their work heavily improves the quality of output. Write end-to-end tests that simulate real user flows and act as the ground truth. Use property-based testing to specify what should never happen and generate thousands of test cases that attempt to break those constraints. Require tests to run quickly and deterministically so that agents retry when the loop is slow or unreliable.

articles.headline: AI Companies Play Cat-and-Mouse With Secret-Stealing Spies

This makes the industry ripe for espionage. While the companies have been on guard against the threat, there's no such thing as a perfect defense. This article explores the different ways corporate espionage is happening in the AI industry.

articles.headline: CASTLE: training natural language search before the first real query
articles.blurb: Cold-start natural-language search often lacks both real queries and relevance labels. Airbnb's CASTLE jointly generates synthetic queries and labels from de-identified booking sessions. Its queries matched real guest query patterns much better than baselines, and human reviewers agreed with its relevance labels >90% of the time. Carefully governed behavioral data can bootstrap search training before meaningful traffic exists.

articles.headline: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers
articles.blurb: GitHub built a star history API that returns daily counts without exposing users' identities, cutting React's full history from about 2,500 requests to 24. It reduces database work by filtering stars by date before counting them, rather than repeatedly processing every star.

articles.headline: Zero-downtime Postgres upgrades with logical replication
articles.blurb: Logical replication offers a practical path to near-zero-downtime PostgreSQL major upgrades, with live rollback enabled by reverse replication. A Docker-based demonstration ran old and new clusters in parallel, freezing writes and waiting for replication to catch up before cutover. It achieved 181 ms of write interruption during upgrade and 179 ms during rollback, without data loss.

articles.headline: Need to Know: Implementing row-level security for Claude Dashboards via Model Context Protocol
articles.blurb: This proof of concept shows how to add row-level security to Claude Dashboards using an MCP server to authenticate users and query DuckDB for only the data they can access. Access rules are enforced before data reaches Claude, allowing the same dashboard to show different results for each user.

articles.headline: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
articles.blurb: Cloudflare held back exponential hardware growth by shrinking data earlier and moving duplication later: split monolithic schemas, switch to zstd, send each event once then replicate after sampling, sample at the edge, and pre-aggregate known queries. Optimize bytes, not just compute: prune fields, compress measured workloads, push reductions upstream, and replicate compacted data.

articles.headline: Four PostgreSQL arguments that came out even
articles.blurb: PostgreSQL micro-optimization alternatives often don't matter. For 1,000 IDs, IN, ANY, and VALUES joins perform similarly; prefer parameterized ANY for stable query text. Short text, enums, and smallints use near-identical storage; mostly-NULL columns are cheap. Don't blindly rewrite but EXPLAIN on your own data.

articles.headline: Phoenix (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: Phoenix is a self-hosted, open-source AI observability platform for tracing, evaluating, and debugging LLM applications. It captures OpenTelemetry traces; offers retrieval and response evaluations, versioned datasets, and experiments; and supports prompt testing and replay. Framework- and provider-agnostic instrumentation makes it useful for teams that need to diagnose agent behavior and measure changes before production.

articles.headline: XERJ (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: XERJ is an Apache-2.0, Elasticsearch-compatible local search engine that automatically indexes code, logs, PDFs, SQLite, and CSVs into typed datasets for agent retrieval, incident analysis, and RAG. Its autoindex workflow avoids schema setup and returns ranked passages with file and line locations. The project defaults to local operation, although optional reranking can send text to an external provider.

articles.headline: SQLBuild: safe refactoring for warehouse SQL (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: SQLBuild is an open-source SQL and Python transformation framework for safely changing warehouses. It checks contracts and lineage before execution, runs graph-level tests and production diffs, and lets teams rename incremental models or columns while preserving history and compatibility views. A local DuckDB playground makes it easy to evaluate. Snowflake, Postgres, BigQuery, and Databricks adapters are available.

articles.headline: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
articles.blurb: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion, an in-house version control system built in five months, after daily code merges grew from 2,500 to over 30,000. By moving operations to servers and fetching only the files needed, it reports roughly 100 times faster checkouts and 200 times lower CPU and memory requirements than its previous Git mirror infrastructure.

articles.headline: Parsing JSON at tens of gigabytes per second… in Python
articles.blurb: Daniel Lemire's benchmark processed 7.6 GB of JSON in about 0.12 seconds using fastsimdjson on free-threaded Python across 64 cores, reaching roughly 66 GB/s. The speed comes from running threads in parallel and creating Python objects only for the fields needed, with data already decompressed in memory.

The purchase was financed through its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (SATA), alongside a $208M warrant exercise, with cash reserves growing to $310.3M through the period. Bitcoin holdings expanded 11.2% against a 9.4% rise in effective common share count, benefiting existing shareholders on a per-BTC basis. CEO Matt Cole has targeted second-largest public corporate holder by year-end, though Strive currently trails Metaplanet by 11,227 BTC.

articles.headline: BitMEX Sued in UK for Return of $27M BTC Over Unlicensed Derivatives
articles.blurb: A British software engineer has filed suit against BitMEX operator HDR Global Trading in London's Commercial Court, seeking return of 324.8 BTC (~$27.2M) on the grounds that BitMEX conducted regulated derivatives activity in the UK without FCA authorization. The claim, filed under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, targets 1,053 losing perpetual swap trades across five accounts from 2018 to 2022, arguing those contracts are unenforceable against UK residents who dealt with an unauthorized firm. A deceit claim accompanies the restitution suit, alleging BitMEX knew it lacked authorization while representing to clients it could lawfully trade with them. Barber's legal team at Seladore Legal suggests other UK users entered similar contracts, putting total potential exposure at hundreds of millions of pounds, with BitMEX having closed operations on September 23.

articles.headline: Agent-Native Elixir Stack With x402 Payments and WebMCP
articles.blurb: Regents Labs released an open-source Elixir/Phoenix/Ash stack for building agent-native applications, bundling WebMCP for exposing page tools to AI agents, SIWA for agent-specific authentication and sybil resistance, and x402 stablecoin payments for monetizing agent interactions. The stack separates agent and human identity layers, with Privy handling shared human accounts across five production sites already running the architecture. An open-source bootstrapping template called ash-template lets developers spin up compatible apps with payments, compute, and identity pre-wired, with Elixir chosen over TypeScript/React for cost and horizontal scaling at agent volumes. The platform distributes all revenue from its five properties to $REGENT token stakers, operating without VC backing.

articles.headline: Rain Launches Embedded Stablecoin Wallets, Files for OCC National Trust Charter
articles.blurb: Rain launched embedded stablecoin wallets supporting USDC, USDT, and other assets across 12 chains, including Base and Solana, paired with Rain-issued Visa and Mastercard cards accepted at 175 million merchant locations and USD payouts to 80+ countries. The launch follows Rain's acquisition of stored-value platform Ansa two months ago and an OCC national trust bank charter filing eight days prior, moves that shift the customer relationship away from third-party wallet infrastructure providers like Dynamic, Privy, and Turnkey. Rain's full stack spans card processing via Lithic, Episode Six, and Paymentology, direct Visa and Mastercard scheme memberships via Puerto Rico, and receivables financing through Credit Coop. An approved OCC charter would unlock custody monetization on top of a model that combines stablecoin rails with traditional finance licenses to function as a full-service card issuer.

articles.headline: The Death of the Interface
articles.blurb: Capable LLMs and stablecoin legislation enacted on two continents (the US GENIUS Act, effective January, and Europe's MiCA, now in full force) have converged. As AI agents displace app-based interfaces, today's payment infrastructure breaks down because its risk stack (authentication, fraud, disputes, and liability) assumes a human completing each transaction step, a premise that fails entirely in agent-to-agent commerce. David Marcus proposes "headless money" as the required fix: a stablecoin-settled, API-only payment layer combining embedded wallets, fiat connectivity, and card networks that agents can call without any frontend. Lightspark, which he leads, is building toward this stack, with the commercial logic that whoever controls agent-mediated purchase decisions captures marketplace-level economics rather than the 1-300 bps of a conventional payment rail.

articles.headline: Pair Tokens: Auto-Compounding ERC-20 LP Positions via Uniswap v4 Hooks
articles.blurb: StonkBrokers introduced Pair Tokens, a new ERC-20 primitive built on Uniswap v4 hooks that fuses two underlying assets into a single fungible token representing a full-range liquidity pool position. Unlike standard LP NFTs, Pair Tokens auto-compound through a permissionless compound function that reinvests accumulated trading fees back into the position, removing the need for manual fee harvesting. The ERC-20 format preserves composability, allowing Pair Tokens to be traded onchain, LPed, or integrated with launchpads, while a 10% fee on compounded LP fees funds $STONKBROKER token buybacks. Minting and redeeming are live on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers platform as of October 13.

articles.headline: Aave V4 deposits are concentrated in partner-built hubs

articles.headline: Prediction Market Data Ranks F1 as the Most Dramatically Volatile Sport
articles.blurb: Dragonfly Capital managing partner Haseeb Qureshi applied prediction market data to rank sports by drama, measuring minute-by-minute odds volatility as the metric for suspense rather than scoreboard activity. The methodology treats real drama as outcome probabilities shifting in real-time, discounting action that does not move win probability. F1 ranked first, followed by CS2, soccer, basketball, tennis, American football, and baseball, with golf last by a wide margin. The framework demonstrates prediction markets as a quantitative layer for analyzing real-world phenomena, well beyond their primary use in financial price discovery.

articles.headline: Chasing that 32 ms tail latency in ClickHouse
articles.blurb: Engineers at ClickHouse investigated why simple SELECT queries experienced an unexpected 32 ms tail latency after idle periods on high-RTT networks. They discovered that unbatched metadata packets sent alongside result data quickly exhausted the TCP congestion window after it had been reset to its initial size during idleness. To resolve the issue, ClickHouse implemented application-level batching for these metadata packets, effectively halving the TCP segment count and eliminating the tail latency penalty.
